claims.sectionKey: Contraste acotado entre portugués brasileño y español de Madrid
claims.summary: Nespoli (2021), in a literature-based comparison limited to Brazilian Portuguese and Madrid Spanish, reports that the Portuguese compound ter + participle typically expresses universal perfect (persistence to the present), whereas the Spanish compound may express universal or existential perfect; the two compounds therefore do not behave uniformly, and other verbal forms/adverbials also realize perfect.
